Lobel, Jason William. 2013. Philippine and North Bornean languages: issues in description, subgrouping, and reconstruction. PhD dissertation, University of Hawai'i at Manoa (ch.10 'Subanen reconstructions', pp.303-358; ch.9 fn.3 p.287).
sources.note: Nothing on stress placement in Eastern Subanen or any Subanen language. Ch.10 gives only segmental reflexes for ESUB (Tables 10.4-10.5: *y > j intervocalically, *k > glottal stop, *-d- > r) and a remark (pp.313-314) that in Subanen languages 'phrases sound like single phonological words' with strongly proclitic case markers. Ch.9 fn.3 (p.287, in the Maranao chapter): 'most languages native to Mindanao and areas further south have lost contrastive stress' -- an areal generalization, not a statement about Eastern Subanen. Map 10.1 (p.304) places 'E = Eastern Subanen' by Oroquieta/Ozamis, matchi…

sources.note: 'examined the variations of two Subanen dialects identified as Salugnon and Sibugaynon in terms of lexicon and phonology' and 'attempted to explain the phonetic environments that motivate the variations', quantitative-descriptive method over the 200-item Swadesh list; S's snippets add nine vowels in Salugnon and /h/ absent in Salugnon. Nothing on stress, length, pitch accent or tone is visible in the abstract; no tone statement seen.
